bug_description.original: Heap-use-after-free READ 4 in sc_pkcs15_free_object called from fuzz_pkcs15_decode.c
bug_description.normalized: In the fuzz_pkcs15_decode harness, a sc_pkcs15_object is allocated once before a while-loop that calls PKCS#15 decode entry functions. When a decode function successfully parses attacker-controlled ASN.1 data (returning SC_SUCCESS), the loop body frees the object via sc_pkcs15_free_object but does not reallocate it before the next loop iteration or the post-loop cleanup call to sc_pkcs15_free_object, causing a heap-use-after-free when obj->type is read from the freed region.

source.description: The PKCS#15 decode entry function parses the attacker-controlled ASN.1 buffer via sc_asn1_decode, populating obj->type and obj->data on success and returning SC_SUCCESS, which triggers the while-loop body containing the free.
source.value_from: Fuzzer-provided Data/Size buffer passed as *buf/*buflen to the decode function

sink.description: sc_pkcs15_free_object reads obj->type on the already-freed sc_pkcs15_object via switch (obj->type & SC_PKCS15_TYPE_CLASS_MASK), triggering a 4-byte heap-use-after-free READ.

root_cause.description: After a successful decode, sc_pkcs15_free_object(obj) frees the object inside the while-loop body, but no reallocation of obj (obj = calloc(1, sizeof *obj)) follows before the stale pointer is reused on the next iteration or at the post-loop cleanup.

tainted_value_origin.description: Attacker-controlled fuzzer input Data is aliased to p and passed by reference to decode_entries[i], which parses the ASN.1 content from this buffer.

parser_admitted.description: sc_asn1_decode successfully parses the crafted ASN.1 data without returning an error, causing the decode entry function to populate obj and return SC_SUCCESS.

coarse_trace.summary: Allocates sc_pkcs15_object via calloc, passes attacker-controlled data to PKCS#15 decode functions in a while loop, frees obj on success but never reallocates before reuse, then calls sc_pkcs15_free_object(obj) again after the loop with the stale pointer.
Parses attacker-controlled ASN.1 data, populates obj->type and obj->data, returns SC_SUCCESS enabling the while-loop body that frees obj.
Called twice on the same obj pointer: first inside the while-loop body (freeing the object) and then in the post-loop cleanup (use-after-free), reading obj->type from the freed 2776-byte heap region.

fine_trace.note: Heap-allocates a zeroed sc_pkcs15_object (2776 bytes). This is the sole allocation of obj for this loop iteration of i; no reallocation occurs after it is freed inside the while loop.

The decode function consumes the attacker-controlled buffer via sc_asn1_decode, parsing ASN.1 auth type data. On success, the function proceeds to set obj->type and obj->data, and returns SC_SUCCESS to the caller.

The decode function returned SC_SUCCESS, so the while-loop condition is true and execution enters the loop body. The obj pointer now points to a populated object with obj->type and obj->data set by the decode function.

Frees obj (deallocates the 2776-byte heap region including obj->type, obj->data, and obj->content). After this call, obj is a dangling pointer. The missing reallocation (obj = calloc(1, sizeof *obj)) before the next while-loop condition check or post-loop cleanup is the root cause.
After the while-loop exits (the next decode call fails or no data remains), the post-loop cleanup passes the stale obj pointer (freed at step 4) to sc_pkcs15_free_object.
Dereferences the freed obj pointer to read obj->type (4-byte READ at offset 0 of the freed 2776-byte region). ASan detects this as heap-use-after-free at address 0x61e000001880.

poc.trigger: fuzz_pkcs15_decode receives a 36-byte crafted ASN.1 blob that causes at least one PKCS#15 decode entry function to return SC_SUCCESS, triggering the free-then-reuse path in the while loop.

format.name: ASN.1/DER (PKCS#15 object encoding)
format.contract: A binary blob that when parsed by one of the PKCS#15 decode entry functions (prkdf, pukdf, skdf, cdf, dodf, or aodf) returns SC_SUCCESS at least once, so the while-loop body executes sc_pkcs15_free_object(obj) before the stale pointer is reused.
